title: Ang 711–718: Todi
tomorrow: does a small gift mean a small heart?

cards: Some texts get typed and deleted. The one that says, I'm going to miss you, feels like too much, so it turns into 'lol see you sunday.' Todi, a raga sung in the morning, opens on ang 711 without deleting anything.
Guru Ram Das: without the Lord, my mind can't go on. My Beloved is my very breath.

teach.h: MY MIND CAN'T LIVE WITHOUT YOU.
teach.b: In paraphrase, the hymn on ang 711 says: without the Lord my mind cannot live. My Beloved is my breath of life. The Guru has brought us together, and I won't be thrown back into the frightening ocean again.
No polish, no distance. Todi's pages are few, from ang 711 to 718, and its hymns stay this close. Then near the end, Namdev, on ang 718, teases the people who argue about where God is.
In paraphrase: some say he's near, some say far.

teach.h: NAMDEV: A FISH UP A PALM TREE?
teach.b: You might as well say a fish climbed a date palm. Why talk such nonsense? Put the two together and you get the shape of tender in these pages.
It isn't a debate about how close the Beloved is. It's saying plainly: I can't do without you. And this matters for an ordinary week.
Tender doesn't mean weak, and it doesn't mean dramatic. Guru Ram Das doesn't make a speech.
He says the true, soft thing, once, in the morning, before the day gets loud.

how: Todi is one of the ragas of the Guru Granth Sahib; in kirtan its hymns, such as Guru Ram Das's 'my mind cannot live without the Lord', are traditionally sung in the morning.

games.q: your best friend got into a college far away. at her goodbye party you could crack jokes all night, or say one honest thing. what fits Todi?
o: keep it light: tender words only make goodbyes harder.
say the plain, true thing once: i'll miss you.
save it for a long letter later, when it's less awkward.
games.why: Guru Ram Das doesn't make a speech; he says it once: without you my mind can't go on. tender isn't weak, and it isn't dramatic.

practice: Bring to mind one person you'd miss if they moved away. Hold their face for the sit, and let whatever comes up be there, unhurried. If a true line for them takes shape, keep it; it's yours to send or keep.
